question: Why do Tay-Sachs (HEXA), CLN3 disease and Krabbe disease (GALC) still have no approved disease-modifying therapy, while nine of the twelve family members do?
what_is_missing: No FDA label was found for any HEXA, CLN3 or GALC product (openFDA searched by brand for every approved lysosomal product in this family).
CLN3: an open-label miglustat study states 'No disease-modifying treatments are currently available' (PMID:40924969); n=6, historical controls.
HEXA: only pyrimethamine (phase I/II, dose-limited by side effects; PMID:20926324, PMID:21185210) and a two-patient intrathecal AAV expanded-access report (PMID:35145305).
GALC: haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the only disease-modifying option and works only when done early (PMID:27638597).
searched: openFDA drug label API (brand names for 19 approved lysosomal products)
PubMed: CLN3[tiab] AND miglustat
PubMed: pyrimethamine[ti] AND (Tay-Sachs OR GM2 OR hexosaminidase)
PubMed: (Tay-Sachs[ti] OR GM2[ti]) AND AAV AND gene therapy AND patients
PubMed: Krabbe[ti] AND (cord blood OR transplantation) AND infantile
ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 query.cond: Tay-Sachs Disease, GM2 Gangliosidosis, CLN3 Disease, Juvenile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis, Krabbe Disease, Globoid Cell Leukodystrophy
how_to_find_out: All three are dominated by brain disease, which intravenous enzymes cannot reach (cluster:lysosomal-bbb-barrier). Track the registered CNS-directed gene-therapy and small-molecule trials linked to these diseases in the atlas; ask the patient organisations (NTSAD, Beyond Batten, Hunter's Hope) about programmes not yet registered.

question: What treats the brain disease in the neuronopathic forms of diseases whose approved enzymes only treat the body (Gaucher types 2/3, ASMD type A, MPS I Hurler, neuronopathic MPS II)?
what_is_missing: The current Cerezyme label covers only non-CNS manifestations of type 1 or type 3 Gaucher disease; the Xenpozyme label only non-CNS manifestations of ASMD.
Laronidase does not cross the blood-brain barrier (PMID:15895714).

The brain-penetrant options found are clinical-stage only: ambroxol for neuronopathic Gaucher (systematic review, PMID:39116528) and pabinafusp alfa for MPS II (phase 2/3, PMID:33038326). Any regulatory approval of pabinafusp alfa was not verified from a fetched label, so it is recorded as stage 'clinical'.
searched: openFDA labels: CEREZYME, VPRIV, ELELYSO, XENPOZYME, ELAPRASE (ALDURAZYME returned no openFDA label)
PubMed: laronidase AND ("blood-brain barrier" OR "central nervous system") AND (Hurler OR "MPS I")
PubMed: ambroxol[ti] AND Gaucher AND chaperone
PubMed: pabinafusp[ti]
PubMed: "enzyme replacement therapy" AND "blood-brain barrier" AND "lysosomal storage" AND review[pt]
how_to_find_out: Follow the CNS-directed studies linked to these diseases (e.g. NCT04573023 and NCT05371613 for MPS II); check PMDA (Japan) and EMA records for pabinafusp alfa, which the atlas could not fetch as a label.

question: Which variants in GBA1, HEXA, NPC1 and GAA are 'amenable' to a chaperone, the way GLA variants are classified for migalastat?
what_is_missing: Only GLA has a regulator-accepted variant-level amenability test (the GALAFOLD label restricts use to an amenable GLA variant 'based on in vitro assay data').

For GBA1 (ambroxol), HEXA (pyrimethamine) and NPC1 (arimoclomol) the evidence is per drug, not per variant; for ambroxol the chaperone action itself is questioned for some variants (PMID:38797393), and the arimoclomol label says its mechanism in NPC is unknown.
Our variant_group nodes are ClinVar consequence classes (e.g. 574 GLA missense P/LP records), not functional amenability classes.
searched: openFDA label GALAFOLD, MIPLYFFA
PubMed queries listed under the migalastat, ambroxol, pyrimethamine, NPC1 I1061T and GAA chaperone claims (pipeline/families/lysosomal/curation.py)
ClinVar esearch/esummary per gene
how_to_find_out: A cross-gene, variant-level table of misfolding readouts (ER retention, stability, response to chaperone in patient cells), like the one regulators accepted for migalastat. The same table would also test the cross-family bridge to SLC6A1, where about a third of loss-of-function missense variants reach the surface and are outside a chaperone's reach (PMID:38781976).

question: What does the CLN3 protein do, and what exactly is stored?
what_is_missing: CLN3 is a lysosomal membrane protein, not an enzyme; we found no curated statement of its molecular function, so disease:CLN3 has no enzyme-deficiency or loss-of-function mechanism edge, only lysosomal storage (PMID:27491213).
GO annotations for CLN3 are mostly inferred (IEA/ISS), apart from lysosomal lumen acidification and lysosomal transport (IMP).
searched: PubMed: CLN3[ti] AND (Batten OR "neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis") AND lysosom* AND review[pt]
QuickGO annotations for UniProtKB:Q13286 (16 candidate processes)
how_to_find_out: Recent structural and lipidomic studies of CLN3 (not yet curated here) should be reviewed by a biochemist before a mechanism edge is added.

question: Do lysosomal and SNAREopathy disorders overlap in symptoms enough to be confused clinically?
what_is_missing: With the same method and thresholds as the SNAREopathy layer (Resnik BMA, >= 95th percentile for both diseases and >= 99th for one), no cross-family pair qualified.

Near misses in the top 5% of both backgrounds: GALC-UNC13A (97.1/97.4%), GBA1-UNC13A (96.9/97.3%), TPP1-STXBP1 (96.5/95.7%), ARSA-STXBP1 (96.7/95.3%), GAA-SYT2 (96.0/95.8%: two causes of neuromuscular weakness). They are recorded in data/raw/families/lysosomal/hpo_stats.json, not drawn as edges.
searched: phenotype.hpoa 2026-09-02 / hp.obo 2026-09-01; SNAREopathy profiles from data/raw/biology/hpo_stats.json
how_to_find_out: A clinician review of the near-miss pairs (e.g. whether CLN2 disease enters the differential of early-onset epileptic encephalopathy alongside STXBP1, which would argue for including TPP1 in epilepsy gene panels).

question: How should GBA1's role in Parkinson disease be represented?
what_is_missing: Monarch records GBA1 -> late-onset Parkinson disease and Lewy body dementia as 'contributes_to' (OMIM), and Orphanet as 'Major susceptibility factor in' (ORPHA:411602). These are susceptibility links, so they are excluded from the GBA1 umbrella's subtypes and causes edge (listed in attrs.excluded_susceptibility_links).
searched: Monarch v3 CausalGeneToDiseaseAssociation and CorrelatedGeneToDiseaseAssociation for HGNC:4177
Orphadata rd-associated-genes ORPHA:411602
how_to_find_out: If the atlas adds a Parkinson disease family, link it to gene:GBA1 with a susceptibility relation rather than 'causes'; the ambroxol chaperone work spans both (PMID:38797393).

question: Which lysosomal communities lack a verified patient organisation, registry or research group in the atlas?
what_is_missing: CLN2 (TPP1): only one verified organisation (Noah's Hope); CLN3 organisations other than Beyond Batten name only the umbrella 'Batten disease'.
No registry page was verified for Gaucher, Fabry, Tay-Sachs, MPS II or MLD (registry studies found on ClinicalTrials.gov are included as assets instead).

No research group met the threshold (>= 2 senior-author papers among the 80 most recent title-matched papers) for Gaucher, MPS I or MPS II: the literature is spread over many groups. NIH RePORTER was not searched for this family.
ARSA: No MLD registry or natural-history study described on stored pages.
CLN3: No CLN3-specific registry found; Batten-wide BDCRC network and natural-history study recorded from the URBC page (umbrella term 'Batten disease').
GAA: No Pompe registry description was stored: IPA ('Pompe Registry') and AMDA ('Patient Registry') mention one only as menu links; the MDA Pompe page returned HTTP 404.

GALC: No Krabbe registry described explicitly; KrabbeCURES recorded as a research-participation platform. Partners for Krabbe Research (p4kr.org) and Legacy of Angels (legacyofangels.org) did not resolve (DNS).
GBA1: No Gaucher registry or natural-history study is described on the stored pages (Gauchers Association lists research projects such as Rapsodi and Gaucherite only as menu links).
GLA: No Fabry registry or natural-history study described on stored pages; National Fabry Disease Foundation (fabrydisease.org) fetch failed (HTTP 307 redirect loop).
HEXA: No GM2/Tay-Sachs registry description stored (CATS Foundation lists a 'Registry' only as a menu link).
IDS: No MPS II-specific registry or natural-history study described on stored pages; MPS Society Australia fetch failed (connection refused).
searched: Organisation websites listed in pipeline/families/lysosomal/web_sources.json (stored under data/raw/families/lysosomal/web/)
PubMed title searches in data/raw/families/lysosomal/research/<GENE>.esearch.json
ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 condition searches (titles with Registry / Natural History / Outcome Survey)
how_to_find_out: Search NIH RePORTER per disease (pipeline/community/fetch_reporter.py shows how), widen the PubMed window for Gaucher and MPS, and ask the umbrella groups (BDSRA, National MPS Society, NTSAD) for registries they run.
